examples.text: Yiddish is a High German language […] two varieties of Yiddish developed […]
examples.ref: 1983, Philip Baldi, An Introduction to the Indo-European Languages, page 128:

glosses: A West Germanic, or more specifically High German, language that developed from Middle High German dialects, with an admixture of vocabulary from multiple source languages including Hebrew-Aramaic, Romance, Slavic, English, etc., and mostly written in Hebrew characters which is used mainly among Ashkenazic Jews from central and eastern Europe.
